$description: Semantic roles, dark theme. This is the layer application code is allowed to use. A role names the job a value does, so re-theming means re-pointing these and nothing else.

surface.$description: Two-pole ladder: the well behind cards is the darkest plane, chrome sits one step up, and raised content reads brighter than the void behind it.

page.$description: Body, the content well behind cards

inert.$description: Chart grid, track fills, skeleton states

subtle.$description: Tint wash over an unknown surface: nav items, chips, zebra rows

scrim.$description: The backdrop behind a modal or drawer: the page colour at 80%, so what is underneath stays legible as context and the raised surface reads as the only lit plane.

content.$description: Text and icons, loudest to quietest. Every role except disabled meets WCAG AA on every surface in the ladder.

disabled.$description: Disabled controls. Exempt from AA per WCAG 1.4.3, and never the only signal that a control is off.

border.$description: Hairlines, not weight. Translucent so they read correctly over any surface in the ladder.

default.$description: Card and input edges, the default

control.$description: The edge of a control whose edge is the whole affordance: an unchecked checkbox or radio, a switch track, the outline of a chart track. 3:1 on every surface (WCAG 1.4.11). Not for cards, inputs or dividers.

accent.$description: Active tab underline, focused input, selected row rail

focus.$description: The focus ring colour, for an outline where a component already carries a ring or shadow. Otherwise the ring is shadow-focus.

accent.$description: One saturated hue in the whole system. Sparing use is what makes it read as signal. The fill carries a white label at AA; text has its own tinted step because the fill reaches only 3.85:1 on surface-card.

default.$description: Accent icons, borders, active nav indicators

hover.$description: Hover for accent icons and links

text.$description: Accent-coloured text and links, and the active nav marker bar. Tinted because the product accent reaches only 3.85:1 on surface-card.

fill.$description: Primary button background. White on it is 4.50:1.

fill-hover.$description: Primary button hover: the fill at 90%, so it lightens slightly over its backdrop. White on it is 4.0:1 over light surfaces, a documented exception, and 5.2:1 over dark ones.

subtle.$description: Active nav item pill, selected row: accent text at 20%

gradient.$description: The logo gradient. Marks and rules only, nothing on top of it.

gradient-fill.$description: Banner gradient: the logo's end colours with the accent fill held across the middle, where the text sits. White text only on the solid band.

status.$description: Eight roles per state. `default` is the hue as a graphic (dot, glyph, progress fill) at 3:1 on every surface it sits on, including its own chip. `chart` is the hue as a chart segment, which on light is lighter still and holds 2:1 on the card, its reading carried by a legend or label. `text` is the label on a normal surface at 4.5:1. `fill` is a solid badge or button background with `on-fill` as its label, and on dark it is also the 3px edge on large status surfaces. `subtle` and `subtle-border` are a status chip: `text` on a pastel with a faint edge of the same hue. `surface` and `border` are a large status surface (callout, banner, tile). On dark those are neutral, and the state is carried by a 3px edge in `fill`, because a tinted dark surface cannot get light enough without costing the text on it contrast. Body text on a large surface stays content-default; the title takes `text` and the icon `default`.

chart.$description: The state as a chart segment, beside a legend or label that carries the number. On light it is lighter than `default` so a chart reads as one family with the series; on dark it is `default`.

on-fill.$description: Dark label. The warning fill is too light for white.

default.$description: A true red, separate from the crimson accent.
Neutral grey. The brand has no blue.

subtle.$description: Neutral chips are the hover grey, with no edge.

surface.$description: Info is neutral in both themes and takes no edge.

series.$description: Categorical data colours: chart series in this order, and the marker dot on a category chip. Graphics only: never a text colour, never a chip fill, never a status. On light a chart fill holds 2:1 on the card and is always named by a legend or label; on dark every series clears 3:1. A label drawn on a series fill takes on-series of the same number. Past six series, label every one; past eight, fold the tail into 8.

on-series.$description: The label on a series fill, one per series: a segment of a stacked bar wide enough to name itself. Each reaches 4.5:1 on its series. On dark every series is light and takes the dark label; on light the deeper series take white and the lighter ones a dark label.

syntax.$description: Syntax highlighting in code blocks, editors and diffs. Text at 4.5:1 on the surfaces code sits on. Green and red are never syntax colours: in a diff they mean added and removed, and a token in either would read as a change. The accent stays out too, so a string never looks like a link.

plain.$description: Scalars and anything the grammar leaves unscoped.

key.$description: Mapping keys, properties, tags and attribute names: the structure a reader scans first.

constant.$description: Numbers, booleans, null, and language constants.

keyword.$description: Keywords, operators with a name, and YAML anchors and tags.

comment.$description: Comments, set in italic. Secondary rather than muted, because comments also sit on the tinted lines of a diff and have to stay at 4.5:1 there.

highlight.$description: Fills that sit behind text that still has to be read: a search match, wherever text is searched, and the added and removed lines of a diff. Every syntax token and every content step reaches 4.5:1 on each of them.

match.$description: The fill behind a search match, in code and in a table or list: a deep blue that keeps every syntax token at 4.5:1. The outline, not the fill, is what makes a match findable.

match-border.$description: The 1px outline of a search match, at 3:1 on the surfaces text sits on.

added.$description: The tint on an added line in a diff. Its lightness is capped by the quietest syntax token, so it differs from the card by hue rather than by brightness.

added-emphasis.$description: The changed words within an added line: the same lightness as the line tint at three times the chroma, so it reads as more green rather than as lighter.

removed.$description: The tint on a removed line in a diff.

removed-emphasis.$description: The changed words within a removed line.

shadow.$description: Deeper on near-black surfaces than they would be on light, because elevation cannot be read from brightness alone here.

focus.$description: Focus ring. Never removed without a replacement.
